subject: Transportation Systems
title: Piracy in Modern Shipping
description: A short lesson to help you apply Piracy in Modern Shipping.

hook.text: Piracy isn't history. In the early 2010s, Somali pirates hijacked hundreds of ships for ransom.

buildup.text: Armed men in small speedboats would board slow-moving cargo ships in the Gulf of Aden.

discovery.text: Ransoms totaled hundreds of millions of dollars. Insurance premiums for the region skyrocketed.

twist.text: International naval patrols, armed guards, and faster routing slashed successful attacks dramatically.

climax.text: Southeast Asian waters and West Africa now see more piracy incidents than East Africa.

punchline.text: Pirates still operate. They just moved.

quiz.question: What reduced Somali piracy?
options: Naval patrols, armed guards, and rerouted shipping
